question: In structural equation models estimated with small samples, how does Bayesian estimation compare with frequentist (maximum likelihood) estimation in terms of performance, accuracy, and bias?
eligibility: The study concerns a structural equation model or a model in the SEM/latent-variable family (CFA, latent growth/class, multilevel, mediation).
The study investigates Bayesian estimation (with prior distributions / MCMC) of such a model.
Performance of Bayesian estimation is compared against frequentist / maximum-likelihood (or alternative) estimation.
The estimation problem is set in a small-sample (or few-cluster) context.
Estimator performance is evaluated via a Monte Carlo / simulation study (optionally alongside an empirical example).
A peer-reviewed methodological paper in the field of the social/behavioural sciences.
as_of_source: day after the latest Entrez date among gold records (a lower bound on the review's search date)
source: SYNERGY dataset (asreview/synergy-dataset) Smid_2020; social-science methodology review 'Bayesian Versus Frequentist Estimation for Structural Equation Models in Small Sample Contexts' (Struct Equ Modeling 2020, doi:10.1080/10705511.2019.1577140); gold = label_included==1 rows with DOI, resolved via [AID]
